paper_title: Attributing Response to Context A Jensen-Shannon Divergence Driven   Mechanistic Study of Context Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
caption: Computational efficiency comparison between our ARC-JSD and Contextcite (n=256 calls) across all datasets and RAG models. Each bar represents the average seconds per sample for ARC-JSD and Contextcite with different RAG models and datasets.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled "Computational Efficiency: ARC-JSD vs. Contextcite" compares the average processing time in seconds per sample for two methods—ARC-JSD and Contextcite—across four different RAG models (Qwen2-1.5B-IT, Qwen2-7B-IT, Gemma2-2B-IT, Gemma2-9B-IT) and three datasets (TyDi QA, Hotpot QA, MuSiQue). The horizontal axis lists the models in the order presented, while the vertical axis, labeled "Seconds/Sample," ranges from 0 to 80 with major gridlines at intervals of 20. Each group of bars corresponds to a model, with three pairs of bars per group: one pair for each dataset. Within each dataset group, the first bar (darker blue or orange) represents ARC-JSD, and the second (lighter blue or orange) represents Contextcite. The legend indicates the color coding: dark blue for ARC-JSD on TyDi QA, orange for Contextcite on TyDi QA, light blue for ARC-JSD on Hotpot QA, light orange for Contextcite on Hotpot QA, very light blue for ARC-JSD on MuSiQue, and very light orange for Contextcite on MuSiQue. For all models and datasets, Contextcite consistently requires more time than ARC-JSD. The most significant difference is observed in the MuSiQue dataset with the Gemma2-9B-IT model, where Contextcite takes approximately 80 seconds per sample, while ARC-JSD takes around 15 seconds. In contrast, for Qwen2-1.5B-IT on TyDi QA, both methods are relatively fast, with ARC-JSD at about 2 seconds and Contextcite at about 5 seconds. The bars are arranged in groups by model, with datasets ordered as TyDi QA, Hotpot QA, MuSiQue within each group, and the chart uses a clean, grid-based layout without additional annotations or emphasis on specific bars.
